components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

All 12 tests pass. The change is complete.

## Summary

The `initials` field is a computed, read-only property on the `Owner` response, so I mirrored the existing `displayName` pattern:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added an `initials` property to the `Owner` schema (read-only string), which drives generation of the `OwnerDto` field.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added a MapStruct `@Mapping` expression on `toOwnerDto`:
   ```java
   @Mapping(target = "initials",
       expression = "java(Character.toUpperCase(owner.getFirstName().charAt(0)) + \".\" + Character.toUpperCase(owner.getLastName().charAt(0)) + \".\")")
   ```
   This produces the upper-cased first letters of `firstName` and `lastName`, dot-separated with a trailing dot (e.g. `john smith` → `J.S.`).

The new `Cp06Tests` and all 11 existing acceptance tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 12 tests, 0 failures).
